title: Liskov substitution
summary: A subtype must keep every promise its base type makes. The Square/Rectangle trap and how to avoid it.

steps.title: The promise of a base type
body: The **Liskov Substitution Principle (LSP)**: code written against a base type must keep working when handed **any** subtype.
If `Bird` has `Fly()` and `Penguin : Bird` throws `NotSupportedException` from it, every loop over birds is a landmine. The type system said "this is a bird, birds fly", and the subtype lied.
Inheritance is a promise of *behaviour*, not just of method names.

steps.prompt: `class ReadOnlyList : MyList` overrides `Add` to throw `NotSupportedException`. Why is that a problem?
options: Code that accepts a `MyList` and calls `Add` will crash when given a `ReadOnlyList`
It is not a problem; it is the intended design of inheritance

steps.title: The Square/Rectangle trap
body: Mathematically a square *is a* rectangle. So:
```csharp
class Rectangle
public virtual int Width { get; set; }
public virtual int Height { get; set; }
public int Area => Width * Height;
class Square : Rectangle
public override int Width  { set { base.Width = base.Height = value; } }
public override int Height { set { base.Width = base.Height = value; } }
Now someone writes perfectly reasonable code for rectangles. Step through it with a `Square`:

code: public virtual int Width { get => _w; set => _w = value; }
public virtual int Height { get => _h; set => _h = value; }
public override int Width { get => base.Width; set { base.Width = value; base.Height = value; } }
public override int Height { get => base.Height; set { base.Width = value; base.Height = value; } }
public virtual int Width { get => _w; set => _w = value; }
public virtual int Height { get => _h; set => _h = value; }
public override int Width { get => base.Width; set { base.Width = value; base.Height = value; } }
public override int Height { get => base.Height; set { base.Width = value; base.Height = value; } }
steps.explain: Anyone who set width 5 and height 4 expects 20. The `Square` silently broke the rectangle's promise that width and height change independently.

steps.prompt: What is the root cause of the Square/Rectangle bug?
options: `Rectangle` promises that `Width` and `Height` are independent, and `Square` cannot keep that promise
`Area` should be a method, not a property

steps.title: Fixing it
body: Two common cures:
1. **Do not inherit.** Make both implement a smaller promise they can both keep:
```csharp
interface IShape { int Area { get; } }
record Rectangle(int Width, int Height) : IShape { public int Area => Width * Height; }
record Square(int Side) : IShape { public int Area => Side * Side; }
2. **Make them immutable.** The bug needed setters. Without mutation, "a square is a rectangle with equal sides" is harmless.
Signs of an LSP violation: a subclass that throws `NotSupportedException`, overrides a method to do nothing, or callers that check `if (x is Square)` before using a `Rectangle`.

steps.prompt: Does the subtype honour its base type?
items: `FileLogger` and `ConsoleLogger` both implement `ILogger.Log` by writing the message
`CachedRepository` returns the same data as the real one, just faster
`SortedList` keeps every item you `Add`, in order

steps.title: Escape the trap
prompt: Rewrite the shapes so no subtype can break another's promise:
`Square` must **not** inherit from `Rectangle`, and there must be no setters.
starter: public virtual int Width { get => _w; set => _w = value; }
public virtual int Height { get => _h; set => _h = value; }
public override int Width { get => base.Width; set { base.Width = value; base.Height = value; } }
public override int Height { get => base.Height; set { base.Width = value; base.Height = value; } }
solution: record Rectangle(int Width, int Height) : IShape
template: Dojo.Check("Square is not a Rectangle", !typeof(Rectangle).IsAssignableFrom(typeof(Square)), "Square still inherits from Rectangle");
Dojo.Eq("a wider rectangle via with", 24, (new Rectangle(5, 4) with { Width = 6 }).Area);
